title: Israeli Strike in Khan Younis Kills Hamas Rafah Brigade Commander, Hamas Confirms
dek: Israel’s military and Shin Bet say they killed a senior Hamas commander in a drone strike; Hamas confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis. Gaza’s Health Ministry reported 16 killed in 48 hours.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Destroyed buildings along al-Seqaly Street in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, in June 2024 (file photo)

keyPoints: Israel’s military and the Shin Bet security agency said in a joint statement that they targeted a senior Hamas military commander in a drone strike in Khan Younis on Saturday, Al Jazeera reported.
Hamas confirmed that Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in an Israeli strike on the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, Al Jazeera reported.
Gaza’s Health Ministry said in its latest update on Saturday that Israeli attacks killed 16 people and injured 68 over the previous 48 hours, according to Al Jazeera.
AP described the strike as an overnight airstrike; Al Jazeera reported a Saturday strike. Meridian has not resolved that difference in timing.
Meridian has not independently verified the ministry’s figures or either side’s account of the target.
body:
Israel’s military and the Shin Bet security agency said in a joint statement that they had targeted a senior Hamas military commander in a drone strike in Khan Younis on Saturday, Al Jazeera reported. Hamas later confirmed that the man killed was Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade. In a statement early Sunday, Hamas said he was a senior member of its military wing.

## The strike

Al Jazeera reported that the strike hit the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, a coastal zone crowded with displaced Palestinians living in tents. Its report said the strike hit a tent sheltering displaced people and wounded two others, who were taken to Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, according to medical personnel. Al Jazeera said it had verified video, posted by Palestinian journalists, showing ambulances inside the hospital grounds.

The Associated Press, in its Sunday Mideast roundup, described the strike as an overnight airstrike on southern Gaza and reported that Israeli forces had killed a top Hamas commander. Al Jazeera described the strike as a Saturday drone strike. Meridian has not resolved that difference in timing.

## Health Ministry toll

Gaza’s Ministry of Health said in its latest update on Saturday that Israeli attacks had killed 16 people and injured 68 others over the previous 48 hours, Al Jazeera reported. Citing the ministry, Al Jazeera said Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,643 Palestinians and injured 5,964 since the ceasefire took effect on Oct. 11, 2025, and that at least 850 bodies have been recovered from under rubble. The ministry’s cumulative count since October 2023 is 74,695 killed and 176,093 injured. These are the ministry’s figures as reported; Meridian has not independently verified them.

The ministry also reported that deaths related to cold had risen to 11 after a nine-month-old baby died from hypothermia, Al Jazeera said.

## Wider context

Anadolu reported that Türkiye and 17 other countries strongly condemned an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis that caused casualties among patients and medical personnel. They urged Israel to uphold the ceasefire and allow unrestricted delivery of humanitarian aid. Anadolu also reported, citing medical sources, that an Israeli drone strike killed a Palestinian and wounded two others in southern Gaza, amid what it described as continued violations of the ceasefire agreement.

Al Jazeera reported that Israel has repeatedly attacked the al-Mawasi area despite previously designating it a humanitarian zone. The sources Meridian reviewed do not include published evidence from Israel’s military or Shin Bet for the target’s role. Hamas’s confirmation describes him as a senior member of its military wing.
